title: The Quran: Surah 17, al-Isra' (The Night Journey)
author: Tradução inglesa de Talal Itani (ClearQuran)
tradition: Texto sagrado do Islão, século VII
intro: Lição sobre a Surata 17. O texto inglês é a tradução de Talal Itani, reproduzida sem alterações; as notas de língua, perguntas, discussão e escrita são material pedagógico separado, baseado apenas no que o próprio texto diz. Cada nível estuda um excerto diferente.

source.title: Quran English Translation: Clear, Pure, Easy to Read Modern English
source.edition: Edition A (uses the word 'Allah' to refer to the Creator)

questions.q: According to verse 23, what should you not say to your parents?
questions.why: O versículo 23 diz: 'do not say to them a word of disrespect'.

options: to speak angrily to someone because of something they did
questions.why: 'Scold' é repreender ou ralhar com alguém.

questions.q: The verse says 'If either of them or both of them reach old age with you'. When does this advice matter most?
options: When the parents are far away
questions.why: A frase 'reach old age with you' mostra que o conselho se aplica quando os pais envelhecem.

questions.q: Which pair of ideas does the verse put side by side?
options: Disrespect and scolding, against kind words
questions.why: O versículo diz o que não fazer (palavra de desrespeito, repreender) e o que fazer (kind words).

questions.q: Which sentence best sums up the verse?
options: It asks the reader to travel with his parents
It asks the reader to give money to his parents
Besides the command to worship none but Him, it asks for kindness towards parents, above all in old age
It asks the reader to ask his parents for advice
questions.why: O versículo começa com o mandamento sobre adorar só a Ele e depois pede bondade para com os pais, sobretudo na velhice.

B2.discussion: The verse asks for kind words, not only for kind actions. Why might the way we speak matter so much when we care for older people?
B2.writing: Write 80 to 100 words: Explain what the verse asks the reader to do and not to do.

questions.q: According to verse 24, what does the speaker say to his Lord about the parents?
options: Have mercy on them, as they raised me when I was a child
questions.why: O versículo 24 diz: 'My Lord, have mercy on them, as they raised me when I was a child.'

questions.q: 'Lower to them the wing of humility' is:
options: an image of gentle and humble behaviour towards them
questions.why: É uma imagem: baixar a asa de humildade em relação aos pais, ou seja, tratá-los com mansidão.

questions.q: In verse 24 the speaker gives a reason for his request: 'as they raised me when I was a child'. What does this link show?
options: That the speaker is still a child
That the care received in childhood is the basis of the request
questions.why: O pedido de misericórdia assenta no cuidado recebido quando era criança.

options: From a prayer to a rule
From rules about behaviour, what to say and not to say, to a prayer in the speaker's own words
From a question to a story
From a story to a list of places
questions.why: O versículo 23 dá regras sobre o que dizer e não dizer; o versículo 24 inclui uma oração entre aspas.

options: It covers what to say to parents and the attitude of humility and mercy behind it
questions.why: O versículo 23 fala das palavras e o versículo 24 fala de humildade e misericórdia.

C1.discussion: Verse 23 gives rules about speech, and verse 24 turns to attitude and prayer. How does adding a prayer change the weight of the rules?
C1.writing: Write 120 to 150 words: Explain how verse 24 develops what verse 23 asks.

questions.q: What does verse 25 say about what is in your minds?
options: No one knows what is in your minds
Your minds are hidden from Him
Your Lord knows best what is in your minds
questions.why: O versículo 25 diz: 'Your Lord knows best what is in your minds.'
'Righteous' descreve quem age de forma recta.

questions.q: Verse 25 follows verses about words and humility with a statement about what is in the mind. What does this link suggest?
options: That the inner state matters alongside outward behaviour
That outward behaviour does not matter
That minds cannot be known by anyone
That the passage has changed topic completely
questions.why: Depois de regras de palavras e de atitude, o versículo 25 fala do que há nas mentes.

questions.q: Which description of the three verses is best supported?
options: A command with details of conduct (23), a prayer (24), and a closing statement about knowledge and forgiveness (25)
questions.why: Cada versículo tem uma função: mandamento, oração e fecho.

questions.q: The passage ends with 'He is Forgiving to the obedient.' What does the ending add?
options: A note of reassurance about forgiveness after the instructions
questions.why: O fecho diz que Ele é 'Forgiving' e acrescenta uma nota sobre perdão depois das instruções.

C2.discussion: The passage moves from outward conduct, through prayer, to what is in the mind. What does this movement from outside to inside do for the reader?
C2.writing: Write 150 to 200 words: Analyse how the three verses move from conduct to prayer to inner state, referring to specific words.
